_comment: Pen-marking motion settings (notes/pen_marking_plan.md, milestone 3+).
home_q: the scan home in UR order [pan, lift, elbow, wrist_1, wrist_2, wrist_3], rad -
the user's elbow-up camera pose (2026-09-24, /joint_states). Its branch is the lock:
every IK solution must keep the signs of lift, elbow and wrist_2 (branch_joints).
standoff_m / clearance_m / roll_step_deg / lin_steps: the approach point above each
tack along the PEN axis; the required gap for the collision model - 3 mm: the tool
envelope already carries margin, and with the tip at 183.78 mm the holder body clears
the plates of a 90 deg T by 3.1 mm at best (63.8 * sin 45 - 42), so 5 mm would refuse
every square fillet; the roll sampling about the pen axis; the number of
Cartesian steps checked on the LIN descent.
work_angles_deg: admissible tilts of the pen off the seam's bisector, in the plane of
the two face normals (rotation about the seam tangent); 0 is the bisector. A 90 deg
corner leaves the holder 7.5 mm from both plates at 0; on plates that lean, a tilt
away from the closer plate is what makes the tack reachable. The best (tilt, roll)
per seam is the one with the largest minimum clearance, then the least joint travel.
transit_clearance_m: the gap kept on FREE moves (tack to tack, home) - larger than the
tack clearance, because a transit has room to spare and the parts sit a few mm off
their model (2026-09-29: a 3 mm transit skimmed the standing plate and hit it at 9 N).
Drops to 90 % of an end pose's own clearance when that is smaller.
max_joint_step_rad: the largest single-joint move allowed between consecutive tack
poses of one seam (no aggressive turns); larger -> the roll is rejected.
table_z_m: null -> the table is the touched plane of table_plane_file
(scripts/table_touchoff.py; 2026-10-02: -96.1 mm at (-0.143, 0.426) m, tilted 1.70 deg,
i.e. about -99.8 mm under the bench parts at (-0.50, 0.08) m). A number here makes it
a horizontal plane at that z instead; table_plane_file null = no table. Before
2026-10-14 table_z_m was null and no plane was used at all: transits ran through it.
departure_m: where transits start and end, along the pen axis (> standoff_m). The pen
moves fast along its own axis between it and the approach point. 2026-10-14: from the
35 mm approach point the planner first had to squeeze out from beside the plate, and
APS's paths round a pipe varied from 0.5 to 1.9 m of tip travel (one swing 0.9 m off);
from 100 mm the same transit came out at 0.19-0.21 m every time, at 3 s.
fixtures: unregistered obstacles (V-blocks, holders, clamps) as boxes in base_link.
Easiest: jog the pen tip to 3-4 corners of a fixture's TOP and note the pendant TCP
x, y, z (m): {"name": "vblock_left", "points_m": [[x, y, z], ...]} - the box is
their smallest rectangle in plan, from the table up to the highest point. Or
explicit: {"name", "centre_m": [x, y, z], "half_m": [hx, hy, hz], "yaw_deg"}.
